text:
olivia: quick spike — POC routing customers to cheaper quantized variants by tier + region. attached sim results. looking for API/console shape + telemetry requirements.
chris: can you drop the sim link or a one-liner summary? what's the observable tradeoff (latency / quality)?
olivia: summary: q4-lite reduces token cost ~2x on avg, median latency +20–30ms. observed quality regression ~4% on our eval set (mostly for long instruction-following prompts). regional note: EMEA capacity constrained, so cheaper variants help a lot there for low-tier customers.
ranit: we will need opt-out/opt-in semantics per account. also want per-account token-cost budget so we can gate admission. how do you see this expressed in API/console?
maya: from console UX POV: per-tenant profile with a small set of presets: Default / Conservative / Frugal. Conservative = only fallback to compatible high-accuracy variants; Frugal = aggressive cheaper variants. also a per-route override toggle.
olivia: API sketch (for account config, not per-request):
```json
{
  "routing_preferences": {
    "profile": "frugal",
    "monthly_budget_usd": "10.00",
    "fallbacks": [
      {"variant": "q4_0", "penalty": 0.2},
      {"variant": "q3_8", "penalty": 0.5}
    ],
    "region_policies": {"eu": {"prefer_cost": true}, "us": {"prefer_latency": true}}
  }
}
```
chris: small API debate: prefer policy at account-level + route-level override. per-request routing_preferences are risky (can be abused to lower quality or beat quota).
olivia: agreed — server-side account policy + opt-in per-request override for power users. telemetry: we must emit `selected_variant`, `fallback_reason`, `estimated_unit_cost`, and `quality_delta_prob` tags per request to metrics and traces.
infra-bot: sim-run: 10k requests across mixed tenants. aggregate cost drop 34% for "frugal" profiles. error/regression spike +1.1% overall, concentrated in <10% of prompt types.
ranit: rollout plan: canary 5% accounts in each region, monitor eval-set regression + production prompt monitors. Add automatic rollback rule: if quality_regression > 2% OR latency_increase > 50ms over baseline for 30m, rollback and notify oncall.
maya: dashboard idea: per-tenant cost delta vs baseline, top-20 prompts with highest quality regressions, and a one-click "pin to no-fallback" action. also surface predicted monthly savings and estimated risk.
chris: token-accounting debate: should quotas/alerts use pre-estimated tokens (predictive admission control) or observed produced tokens? pre-estimate gives better admission control, observed is simpler for billing accuracy.
olivia: proposal: use pre-estimate for admission/routing decisions (so we can refuse/route to cheaper variant before consuming resources) but bill on produced tokens. Add `estimated_tokens` to routing pipeline.
ranit: note: streaming + mid-request fallback is a hard no — fallbacks must be decided before stream start. otherwise we break client contract.
olivia: noted. next steps: implement server-side account policy model + console profile UI + telemetry tags + simulation harness. canary + auto-rollback rules as described. i'll open a design PR that includes sim tables and sample dashboards.
chris: please include the sim harness + metric thresholds in the PR. also add a short customer-facing FAQ that explains tradeoffs and how to opt out.
maya: I'll mock the UI panels and copy for the FAQ. meeting Fri 10am to align.
olivia: thanks — will upload PR and sim results before EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
